ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against the Panamanian National Proceeds and Assets List, UAF Resolution 231/2016 risk matrices, OFAC SDN list, UN Security Council consolidated lists, EU consolidated financial sanctions, and domestic politically exposed persons (PEP) database. Enhanced due diligence for high-risk jurisdictions, PEPs, and unusual wire correlational profiles; immediate termination flag upon unresolved sanctions match.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá – Online Name Clearance / Edicto system (www.registropublico.gob.pa and the platform 'Sistema de Edicto Electrónico')
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company and foundation names must be submitted in the variable Spanish (Castilian) script. Foreign-language names are subject to transliteration to the Latin alphabet; the registrant must produce an exact phonetic transliteration certified by a Spanish-language sworn translator. The name must be unique, not misleading, and cannot imply a sector different from the registered object.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Before expiration, the applicant may file a brief via the Public Registry's electronic gateway requesting renewal for an additional 30-day term (extension) subject to availability. In the event of name rejection, the applicant has 10 business days to file a formal 'Recurso de Reconsideración' with the Director of the Mercantile Registry, after which the Director has 30 days to decide; if still denied, a 'Recurso de Apelación' may be filed before the Pleno of the Comisión de Registro. Failure to act before the reservation window lapses requires a new application and payment.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office arrangements are admissible solely for administrative and legal-registration substance of the Private Interest Foundation (e.g., registered agent address and mailing file). For active implementation of a fast-casual food franchise (ISIC 5610), a physical commercial premises with municipal operational license and health department inspection is non-waivable. The registered office cannot serve as the franchise's public restaurant location.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Physically unannounced inspections by municipal and health authorities for restaurant operations: high probability (≈85% annual audit likelihood); unannounced UAF/Oficio inspection of the foundation's registered office for AML/UBO book-compliance: moderate probability (≈20% in the first year), remote, but substance review may occur without prior notice.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law 25 of 12 June 1995 on Private Interest Foundations (Articles 1-42), as amended; Executive Decree No. 27 of 26 July 1996 (registry rules for PIFs); General Rules and Regulations of the Public Registry of Panama, including Rule No. 4 of 2017 on digital filing; applicable supplementary provisions of the Panama Civil Code on not-for-profit legal persons.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Public Registry of Panama (Registro Público de Panamá) – Special Registry of Private Interest Foundations (Registro Especial de Fundaciones de Interés Privado), Scribal Section No. 5, Arco Iris Building, Panama City.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Foundation Charter (Acta Fundacional / Escritura Pública de Fundación) executed before a Panamanian Notary Public, optionally accompanied by Foundation Regulations (Reglamento); the deed is inscribed in the Special Registry of Private Interest Foundations.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital or escrow deposit applies under Law 25 of 1995. The Founder must assign an initial patrimony adequate for the foundation's lawful purpose; the professional market standard for a PIF used as an operating vehicle is a declared initial endowment of at least USD 10,000, which may be constituted in cash, securities, or movable assets. The Charter states the endowment, which is fully subscribed at formation; the Foundation Council may call or increase contributions by resolution. No bank escrow account is required for incorporation, but the declared endowment must be evidenced when opening bank accounts.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED by the Foundation Council of [Name], incorporated under Panama Law 25 of 12 June 1995: (1) the initial endowment declared in the Foundation Charter is subscribed and acknowledged as constituting the foundation's patrimony; (2) the registered office at the Resident Agent's professional office in Panama City is adopted as the statutory domicile and records seat; (3) the persons named in the Charter are appointed President and Secretary of the Foundation Council, and the Resident Agent is confirmed, each empowered to execute deeds, banking forms, and regulatory filings; (4) management shall obtain all operating licenses for the Chinese Malatang self-serve restaurant activity; and (5) the Treasurer is authorized to open local operating and royalty-collection bank accounts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama – Registry Directorate, Name Review Section (Departamento de Verificación de Nombres, Registro Público de Panamá)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit, through the Resident Agent or directly via the Registry's online platform, at least three proposed foundation names in priority order. The Registry verifies availability and issues a name reservation (validez de nombre) valid for 30 days; the reservation certificate must be annexed to the Foundation Charter deed. The name must conclude with 'Foundation' or the Spanish equivalent and must not coincide with an existing Panamanian entity.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application listing 3 candidate names
Certificate of acceptance of the Resident Agent
Passport or national identity copy of the Founder and of the Foundation Council members
Simplified KYC form for the beneficial owner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the first-choice name is rejected for identity with an existing registration, counsel files a revised reservation with alternate names within 48 hours; the reservation period is renewed upon re-submission.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF), Republic of Panama; official taxpayer portal: https://www.dgi.gob.pa (includes SIE information system and virtual office for RUC management).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Private Interest Foundation (PIF) engaged in Panamanian-source licensor activity must obtain a Registro Único de Contribuyente (RUC) before transacting. Procedure: (1) file the certified foundation charter (Acta de Constitución) registered under Law 25 of 1995 together with the resident agent acceptance deed and identity documents of foundation officers with the DGI; (2) submit the taxpayer enrollment application (Aviso de Inscripción de Contribuyente) via the DGI virtual office, designating the RUC tax regime, economic activity codes (ISIC 5610 / ancillary franchise licensing), and fiscal address; (3) receive the RUC certificate and activate the fiscal registration; (4) register as an ITBMS withholding and transfer taxpayer; (5) where exports will occur, validate the exporter code with the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas. Non-resident founders may act through the Panamanian resident agent; no local director requirement applies to PIFs.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch election exists under Panama law. PIFs are per se separate taxable legal persons created by Law 25 of 1995, taxed under the territorial model only on Panama-source income; foreign-source income is outside the tax net. The foundation may elect the simplified Régimen de Pequeño Contribuyente if annual gross taxable turnover remains at or below B/.36,000, otherwise full ITBMS registration is mandatory. Group consolidation, deemed-dividend, and conduit elections are not available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS - Impuesto a la Transferencia de Bienes Corporales Muebles y la Prestación de Servicios (Panama VAT)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: B/.36,000 (equivalent to USD 36,000) in annual gross taxable turnover; below this threshold a PIF may register as a Pequeño Contribuyente with simplified ITBMS compliance; once the threshold is exceeded, full RUC and ITBMS registration is mandatory under the Código Fiscal.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing through the DGI Facturación Electrónica de Panamá (FEP) system, phased by taxpayer category; billing software must integrate with the DGI via the authorized API/XML schema and transmit invoices in real time for clearance; each e-invoice receives a digital fiscal stamp (sello digital) from the DGI before issuance, and invoices lacking DGI validation cannot support input VAT credits or export zero-rating claims.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A 0% ITBMS rate applies to exports of tangible goods and to services supplied to non-resident persons where the benefit, use, and economic exploitation occur entirely outside Panama. Master franchise licensing royalties collected by the PIF from foreign licensees qualify as zero-rated export services where: (i) the licensee is a non-Panamanian entity; (ii) the intellectual property and brand rights are exploited exclusively abroad; (iii) the master license agreement is notarized and translated and evidences the royalty flow; and (iv) the PIF files the corresponding export service declaration with the DGI. Input VAT attributable to zero-rated supplies is recoverable through periodic ITBMS refund filings.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación) filed with the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas de Panamá
Original or certified Bill of Lading / Airway Waybill evidencing physical dispatch of goods
Inward Remittance Certificate issued by a Panamanian licensed bank evidencing receipt of the royalty wire proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGI audits export zero-rating claims with substance-over-form review of the master license agreement, IP registry filings, and the foreign licensee's operational reality before granting refunds. An unsupported or fraudulent zero-rating claim triggers retroactive assessment of 7% ITBMS on gross royalties, a monthly surcharge of 10% of the unpaid tax, fines of up to 200% of the omitted tax, suspension or cancellation of the RUC, compulsory return of refunded VAT with compound interest, and criminal liability for tax fraud under the Código Fiscal. Panama's dollarized system places no central-bank FX approval requirement on royalty wires, but the inward remittance certificate must evidence receipt within the stated compliance window and match the invoiced amounts.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Republic of Panama operates without a conventional central bank. Banking supervision is vested in the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) under Decreto Ley 2 of 2008; Banco Nacional de Panamá acts as the state's fiscal agent and de facto quasi-central bank for fractional Balboa coin issuance and public-sector clearing, while the US dollar is full legal tender under the 1904 legal-tender decree regime. No separate foreign-exchange commission or central-bank FX licensing body exists.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama is fully dollarized: the Balboa (PAB) is a nominal unit pegged 1:1 to the USD and circulates only as coinage. Capital-account and current-account convertibility are unrestricted; there are no exchange-control permits for inbound capital, no surrender quotas, and no approval gate for outward transfers. Profit remittance, royalty repatriation, and distribution of PIF endowment assets are hurdle-free: foreign-source royalty income generated by the master-licensing model falls outside Panama's territorial tax net, and no withholding or central-bank consent attaches to USD outflows. Residual friction arises exclusively at bank level through AML/KYC documentation, not through FX statute.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Panama imposes no statutory repatriation timeline and no mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts, whether physical goods, services, or royalty receivables. Owing to complete dollarization, 100% of export or royalty proceeds may be retained in USD indefinitely in any SBP-licensed bank account, onshore or offshore, without declaration to a central FX regulator. Only bank-side source-of-funds documentation under Law 23 of 2015 and SBP Acuerdo 004-2019 must accompany the underlying credit.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account — USD Royalty Collection and Disbursement
Capital Escrow Account + Operational USD Account
Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account with Trade Finance Desk
Capital Escrow Account for PIF Endowment

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Medium-Low — admissible only as an ancillary collection layer, never as the primary treasury rail. Panama has no EU-style Electronic Money Institution licence; under Decreto Ley 2 of 2008 only SBP-licensed banks may take deposits from the Panamanian public. Offshore digital EMIs (Wise Business, Payoneer, Airwallex, DLocal-type aggregators) may lawfully facilitate inbound royalty and POS collections, but the PIF must (i) open the EMI in the exact foundation legal name, (ii) attach the Foundation Charter and a notarized Council resolution designating the EMI as a collection channel only, and (iii) effect same-day or next-day USD sweeps to an SBP-licensed bank. Legal constraints: permanent or habitual EMI activity within Panamanian territory requires a banking or money-services licence; US correspondent de-risking increases scrutiny of PIF-to-EMI flows; and SBP risk-based supervision treats unlicensed EMI balances as unregulated liquidity, weakening the evidentiary profile for the PIF's passive-holding and territorial-tax position.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical appearance is effectively mandatory for at least one statutory Council member or the principal beneficial owner at the final account-activation interview in the majority of Panamanian private banks, including Towerbank, Banistmo, and Global Bank. Remote onboarding is available on a discretionary basis when a licensed Panamanian Resident Agent or attorney acts as a trusted introducer, with video-verified KYC accepted for supplemental signatories only. Banco Nacional de Panamá and Caja de Ahorros require physical attendance of the beneficial owner with no meaningful waiver. Under Law 23 of 2015 and SBP Acuerdo 004-2019, banks must identify every natural person exercising effective control; the PIF must deliver the beneficial-owner passport, proof of address, and the Law 254/2021 beneficial-ownership registry receipt even where principals do not travel to Panama.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Perceived opacity of the Private Interest Foundation — historically used for wealth concealment, with no evident commercial substance in the written Charter.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of Foundation Charter and Reglamento as filed in the Public Registry under Law 25 of 1995, with the object clause stating expressly the acquisition and master-licensing of fast-casual Chinese Malatang broth-bowl brand rights and franchise royalty collection; Public Registry certificate of existence; current certificate of incumbency naming all Council members; Panamanian counsel legal opinion confirming PIF validity and economic substance; Law 254/2021 Beneficial Owner Registry filing receipt; signed undertaking to file annual BO updates.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PRC and broader Latin America nexus — brand principal, equipment suppliers, and franchisees resident in China, Colombia, or Mexico, triggering enhanced sanctions/OFAC and FATF-scrutiny flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Comprehensive sanctions-screening report (World-Check or equivalent) covering all Council members, beneficiaries, and contractual counterparties; executed Master License Agreement and Sub-Franchise agreements mapping the royalty waterfall; PRC trademark-registration certificates and brand-licence registry excerpts; supplier invoices and logistics documentation for Malatang self-serve equipment and seasoning; remediation statement confirming Panama's removal from the FATF grey list; internal classification memorandum designating the account as Low_Risk_Standard under SBP Acuerdo 004-2019.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds challenge on the capital escrow — nominal PIF endowment followed by a sudden high-value USD injection from the founder or a non-resident company.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Domiciliary bank reference letter covering the preceding 12 months of the originating account; source-of-wealth questionnaire with supporting evidence such as share-sale deed, dividend distribution certificates, salary and bonus statements, or inheritance and trust-distribution deeds; notarized Council minutes authorising the capital contribution and earmarking the funds for operational liquidity and working capital; complete MT103 wire chain from source bank to the Panamanian receiving account; tax-residence certificate of every funding natural person under CRS.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Recurring cross-border royalty flows with no payroll or physical footprint — red flag for operating an unlicensed money-services business or unauthorized payment facilitator.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master-franchise revenue-share computations certified by an independent accountant; quarterly royalty-invoice files and licensee remittance statements; evidence that the PIF exists solely as a passive intellectual-property holding and licensing vehicle, never in possession of third-party funds; complete SWIFT statement archive; territorial-tax memorandum from Panamanian tax counsel confirming the royalty income classification and non-taxability of foreign-source earnings.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Prior or parallel use of offshore EMI e-wallets before the domestic bank account opening, raising layering and source-of-funds concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written disclosure schedule identifying each EMI platform, account number, and opening date; monthly EMI statements demonstrating immediate sweep-down to the SBP-licensed Panamanian bank; PIF Council resolution appointing each EMI as an auxiliary collection gateway; AML/KYC files received from each EMI; reconciliation evidence showing zero unduly retained or unaccounted royalty funds.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Routing: USD credit via SWIFT MT103 from the founder's or capital-provider's bank to the PIF's demand-deposit account at an SBP-licensed Panamanian bank; settlement occurs over Fedwire/CHIPS through US correspondents such as Citibank N.A. or The Bank of New York Mellon. No prior central-bank authorisation is required in Panama. The receiving bank requires: (i) a completed onboarding KYC file; (ii) an incoming-wire source-of-funds declaration naming the remitter and the foundation; and (iii) a notarized Foundation Council resolution specifying the capital call, the target account, and the intended use (endowment capital versus operating liquidity). Recommended wire-message purpose language: 'Capital contribution to Private Interest Foundation endowment — no goods or services underlying'; where the remitting bank mandates an ISO 20022 ExternalPurposeCode, use 'OTHR' with a full narrative purpose line and avoid goods or services codes. For recurring franchise royalty flows the proper purpose codes are 'ROYA' for royalties and 'LICF' for licence fees, supported by invoices and royalty statements retained in the bank file.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 priority transfers for supplier payments, beneficiary distributions, and professional fees, executed from the Panamanian bank's correspondent network with USD settlement via CHIPS or Fedwire same-day value, with populated fields 50K/59/70 to avoid secondary-correspondent holds; (ii) commercial documentary Letters of Credit under UCP 600 issued by Banistmo, Global Bank, or Citibank for imports of self-serve broth dispensers, Malatang seasoning supply, and kitchen equipment from PRC vendors, structured as sight or deferred-payment LCs supported by commercial invoice, bill of lading, packing list, and certificate of origin; (iii) local POS and card-scheme settlements (Visa and Mastercard) aggregated by the acquiring bank and swept as bulk USD credits to the operational account; (iv) intragroup sweeps from collection sub-accounts using nightly standing-order MT103 instructions. Each outbound disbursement must carry underlying commercial documentation to preserve the PIF's passive-holding character and territorial-tax position; no Panamanian exchange-control filing attaches to any outbound transfer.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/CNH deliverable outright forwards executed offshore with the Panamanian bank's Hong Kong or New York trading desk for contractually fixed CNY-denominated brand and seasoning-supply fees
USD/CNY non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) settling in USD against the CNY fixing differential, compliant for PRC supplier obligations where onshore CNY delivery is unavailable
USD/COP and USD/MXN deliverable FX forwards converting LatAm master-franchise royalty receipts into USD at scheduled intervals
USD/CNY cross-currency swaps under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with credit-support annex, limited to investment-grade bank counterparties and capped at the projected 24-month royalty forecast

Plain-vanilla USD/CNH FX zero-premium collar structures to cap equipment-import costs while preserving downside benefit, permissible without SBP derivatives licensing when executed through an SBP-licensed bank intermediary

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Panama General Directorate of Revenue (Dirección General de Ingresos, DGI)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: June 30 of the applicable calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment accrues a surcharge of 10% of the tax, plus monthly interest of 1%. If unpaid for three consecutive years, the foundation may be administratively struck off from the Public Registry.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Income Tax Return (Declaración Jurada de Renta)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 of the year following the end of the calendar tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a fine of 10% of the tax due (minimum US$50), plus monthly interest of 1% on the unpaid amount, and possible suspension of the Tax Clearance Certificate (Paz y Salvo).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Central Registry of Beneficial Owners (CRB) of Panama, under the DGI
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by June 30, aligning with the annual franchise tax payment; updates within 15 days of any change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file may result in fines of up to US$10,000, together with revocation or suspension of the foundation's certificate of good standing.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A mandatory independent audit is required for entities with annual gross revenue exceeding US$1,000,000 or total assets exceeding US$1,000,000; the threshold applies to foundations conducting Panama-source business. Franchise licensing income below this threshold is not automatically subject to an external audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (International Financial Reporting Standards); the Panama SME standard permits IFRS for Small and Medium-Sized Entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The resident agent is responsible for submitting the annual final beneficial owner (UBO) confirmation electronically to the CRB on or before June 30 of each year. Any change in the foundation's beneficiaries or shareholder-like interests must be filed with the CRB within 15 calendar days.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of Foundation Council Resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$2,500–US$5,000 (only if the compulsory audit threshold is exceeded)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Panamanian Private Interest Foundations (PIFs) are treated as separate taxpayers only for Panamanian-source taxable activities. The standard 25% rate applies to local-source net business income. Qualifying small taxpayers (annual taxable income up to B/.30,000) may elect a 15% preferential scale for the first B/.30,000; no general Panama CIT holiday is available. Industries within the 'Ley de Dictamen' and certain Bicentennial Law incentives may deduct up to 50% of qualifying investment expenditures, but a fast-casual Malatang franchise will not ordinarily qualify for exemption.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 103 (Declaracion Jurada del Impuesto sobre la Renta) - Republic of Panama; filed through the DGI electronic filing system known as 'Sistema de Declaraciones Electronicas' (eTax/DGI).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months after fiscal year-end. For calendar-year taxpayers, the due date is 31 March of the following tax year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year under review, stated as DD/MM/YY - DD/MM/YY.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the PIF's first and final day of its elected fiscal period; if the foundation has no Panamanian-source revenue, still file the corresponding 'no tax due' return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Unique Taxpayer Registry (Registro Unico de Contribuyente) of the foundation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Obtain a provisional RUC from DGI before filing; it is not enough to have a Foundation Public Deed certified.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name of the Private Interest Foundation exactly as registered with the Mercantile Registry.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Council and Resident Agent are responsible; no tax ID from the foreign beneficiary should be inserted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income from Panamanian-source activity; in this case gross franchise receipts, internal royal ticket sales and local Malatang dining revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exclude all foreign-source income properly documented; Panama taxes on a territorial basis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Costos de Ventas / Costos Directos
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct costs of food, preparation, supplies, and self-service staffing; includes cost of imported base broth measured at arm's length.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Transactions with related foreign entities must be justified through Form 3375 and a transfer pricing study.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 - Gastos de Operacion (Ventas y Administrativos)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating expenses: rent, utilities, salaries, local sales agent fees, franchise registration, and DGI withholdings.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments to the overseas Malatang master licensee are expenses only if there is an actual service, substantial evidence and the 12.5% withholding risk is assessed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 - Deducciones de Rentas Exentas / Gastos No Gravables
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Expenses used to produce income not sourced in Panama are not deductible against Panamanian taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Segregate foreign-source costs; a PIF with outward royalty/resale income from offshore units must keep separate accounting.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 - Enajenacion de Acciones u Otros Bienes
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Capital gains on Panamanian shares or local real property, if any; separate section of Form 103.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Gains on foreign assets are not Panamanian-source and are not reported.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 9 - Ingreso Neto Gravable / Perdida Neta
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after all deductions and cost of sales; NOL carryforwards applied up to five years.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Calculate at PIF level; do not claim a tax loss from the underlying foreign investor's own business.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax computed at the applicable rate: 25% standard, 15% on the first B/.30,000 for eligible small taxpayers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The PIF must file and pay; a foreign beneficial owner cannot credibly consolidate Panama tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 11 - Pagos a Cuenta / Creditos por Retenciones
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Monthly advance payments paid during the fiscal year plus third-party withholding certificates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign beneficiaries are not entitled to claim local advance payments unless properly credited to the PIF.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 12 - Impuesto por Pagar o Saldo a Favor
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final amount of tax due after crediting advances and withholding.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any balance due must be paid using DGI tax code 121 by 31 March; a credit balance may be applied to next year or refunded after digital audit.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing and late payment consequences include: monthly surcharge of 5% of the tax due, capped at 50% of the tax, plus statutory interest of approximately 1.5% per month on outstanding balances. Failure to file a zero-due return triggers an administrative fine of B/.250.00 to B/.5,000.00. Penalties also escalate where Form 103 is used as a tool to conceal related-party income, leading to tax adjustment, 25%-50% additional tax, and criminal referral.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% statutory final withholding tax on ordinary dividends declared from Panamanian taxable profits; 20% applies to dividends paid from profits that enjoyed a special exemption or preferential regime.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Panama has a limited DTA network (e.g., Singapore, Korea, Portugal, Spain, France, UK, Italy, Netherlands, UAE, and others). To apply a reduced treaty rate, the non-resident beneficial owner must file Form 202 (Solicitud de Aplicacion de Beneficio de Convenio), submit a valid Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from the treaty partner, and evidence genuine ownership of the shareholding/foundation rights. The Panamanian payer must retain the TRC and disclose the payment in the annual information return; relief is denied if the foundation lacks economic substance in Panama.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 12.5% final withholding tax on gross royalties paid to non-residents for the use of IP in Panama. Interest: statutory 10% withholding tax on interest paid to non-resident lenders and debtholders, subject to treaty reduction to 0%, 5%, or 10% depending on the DTA; repayments of principal are not subject to tax. Where no treaty applies, a gross-up clause must be considered in the master franchise agreement to ensure a net payment.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Panama requires a transfer pricing disclosure form (Formulario 3375) to be filed with the annual income tax return whenever the taxpayer undertakes controlled transactions. A full Local File and transfer pricing study are conventionally expected where related-party transactions exceed B/.500,000 (Balboa, at parity with USD) during the fiscal year. A Master File is expected for multinational groups with consolidated revenues exceeding B/.60 million. These thresholds are applied under Executive Decree 173 of 2004 and Law 7 of 2011, as updated by DGI resolutions.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama does not apply separate Economic Substance Regulations like Barbados or the UAE; however, the territorial tax system imposes an absolute requirement that the PIF demonstrate real business activity in Panama. The PIF Council must keep minutes, manage the Malatang franchise contracts, maintain a registered office, have a resident agent, and keep reliable accounting. If the PIF is instead used merely as a mailbox or isolated treasury vehicle to receive franchise royalties, the DGI will characterise it as a transparent conduit, deny treaty benefits, reallocate income to the foreign beneficial owner, and escalate matters to AML/CRS authorities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately underreporting Panamanian restaurant and franchise revenue, recording ghost expenses from the Chinese Malatang supply chain, or paying actual royalties as fake loans to avoid the 10% dividend withholding tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fine of up to 200% of the omitted tax, monthly interest of 1.5%, plus criminal indictment under Articles 737 and 738 of the Panama Tax Code; penalties are published and the business license is revoked.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The Foundation Council members and the Resident Agent may be pursued personally for the outstanding tax debt if they knowingly signed false returns; criminal imprisonment of up to 5 years is possible, plus a deposit/immigration travel ban.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the PIF solely to hold the Malatang franchise assets while steering sales and management decisions from China or the United States; having no employees in Panama; failure to conduct Council meetings; issuing distributions with no legal documentary trail.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterisation of the PIF as a sham; denial of territorial benefits; all repositioned profits taxed at 25% with 10% surcharge and exchange of information under CRS/FATCA.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly liable to restitution of underpaid taxes and may be disqualified from serving as directors of Panamanian entities for 5 to 10 years; a travel ban is imposed by the DGI Criminal Fiscal Division while the case is investigated.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying for master license fees, broth concentrate, or management services to a related seller at prices exceeding arm's length, without Form 3375, without a local transfer pricing file, or without trade-based economic substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Controlled transaction adjustment by DGI, disallowance of the excessive expense, additional tax at 25%, penalty of 25% of the underpayment or up to B/.150,000 if documentation is missing, plus default interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The council approving inflated invoices is considered a willful accomplice to tax fraud; personal civil liability for the adjusted tax and a 2-year travel ban can be issued.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Self-Serve Malatang store without the required municipal sanitation and consumer protection licenses; handling cash and client payments without anti-money-laundering reporting; or accepting investment from individuals listed on OFAC sanctions lists.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Closure of the establishment, municipal fines up to B/.30,000, revocation of the business license; PIF assets may be frozen and the registered agent is compelled to report violations to the UAF (Unidad de Analisis Financiero).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Foundation Council and senior officers face criminal liability for money laundering up to 12 years' imprisonment; foreign nationals may be deported, and a concurrent travel ban to prevent interregional money movement is issued during investigation.
